originality.rationale: Two primary full texts were inspected with theorem-level comparisons. The 2026 Cartesian-products study explicitly leaves imbalanced three-dimensional Hamming graphs open and provides only a three-colour lower bound here; the 2026 follow-up resolves balanced odd Hamming graphs and expressly identifies unequal-factor products as future questions. Its Lemma 4 does imply the 2q core lower bound via induced embedding; that component is credited as covered, while the attaining partition and equality classification/census are not supplied. Six genuine published-finding corpus queries, historical-claim deduplication, and targeted web searches found no matching exact all-q unequal-factor value or 2q-core classification. Restricted 2012 alliance terminology remains a priority risk; lack of an indexed result is not proof of uniqueness.
residual_risks: A specialized historical defensive-alliance partition formula outside the queried/inspected literature could establish an equivalent result.
The 2012 alliance-partition paper was available in abstract only; its full text was not inspected.
Independent historical-priority and proof audit have not been performed.

value.rationale: The full q>=4 family is an infinite, genuinely imbalanced 3-dimensional Hamming subfamily singled out by a published open problem. It gives the exact maximum majority partition rather than a routine special case of an earlier general formula. Although the 2q bound follows from Lu’s earlier balanced isoperimetric lemma under embedding, the construction attaining the bound on the number of unequal-factor classes and the complete 3q(q+1) equality-case census yield new structural information beyond a known cardinality inequality.
